facts.text: Oxon Hill Manor, the 18th‑century estate that inspired the town’s name, burned in 1895 and was replaced in 1929 by a 49‑room neo‑Georgian home overlooking the Potomac.
The former Oxon Hill Farm and Oxon Cove Park, 800 acres of farmland, transferred to the National Park Service in 1959 and now protect river habitat and structures.
In 1783, John Hanson, the first president of the Continental Congress, died at Oxon Hill Manor, a moment that links the town to early American history.
The Oxon Hill Library Branch houses the Sojourner Truth Room, an African‑American research collection that reflects the community’s commitment to civil‑rights history.
Rosecroft Raceway, founded in 1949, is a local landmark that still hosts harness horse racing and televised simulcast betting events.
